- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 78, true price often drops; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next period if sentiment remains low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 price points if sentiment volatility > 0.2.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.4 to -0.1), model often fails to adjust; delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes or next 3-day window.
